column3: Provenance: in H1' every revealed handle that is a challenger thash or PRF entry has a structured challenger entry at every DSM ancestor of its address (AncOK, part of InvS); the signer reveals a signature only after recomputing its root, whose structure covers every handle of it. Hence a structured challenger request is always answered by its own challenger entry (ask_struct): the canonical value at every address is a challenger draw. On the final table a structured request at b is thashReq tk b (canon b) (struct_val, from canon_kids). Every thash request in the verifier's log is at an address of the forged path its digest selects (verifyLog_path), where the extension left structured entries (ExtS, descent). So on a disagreement-free run a canonical collision is an adversary entry and a structured challenger entry at one address literal with equal truncated values, or a 32-byte key coincidence (canon_split). The pair is charged at the later creation, a fresh tape coordinate, against the earlier value, whatever its visibility; at most one pair per adversary step (pair_count). #(canon ∧ ¬anyDis)·256^(n+32) ≤ R^N·AA·256^32 + R^N·N^2·256^n, and for SPX128f Pr[won] ≤ (JA + 11·AA + 6)/2^128 + (2·S^2 + 3·N^2)/2^256. column2: SPHINCS_SECURITY_CHARTER (query budget of H1 and H1')
column3: Budget A qh qs: on every path of the strategy tree each hash query uses one unit of qh (repeats included; memoization makes this an over-count) and each signing query one unit of qs (legal or not); the output is free. Challenger requests are bounded per routine by closed-form step costs (Cost: steps, adversary steps, entries, adversary entries and challenger h_msg entries on every tape, from every state, for the real and the symbolic run). Entries are the run's distinct draws and each step adds at most one (strace_ents); H1's draws are its entries (runG_draws). Adversary steps of H1' are the adversary's hash queries, the final verification's requests on the adversary oracle (verC) and the extension's h_msg request, so AA = qh + verC + 1, not qh; JA = qh + verC, q = qs, S = kgC + 1 + qh + qs*(signC+1) + verC + extC + 3, N = S + 1. For SPX128f (kgC 4497, signC 370401, verC 11872, extC 117606): JA = qh+11872, AA = qh+11873, S = qh+370402*qs+133979, N = qh+370402*qs+133980, and Pr[won] <= (12*qh + 142481)/2^128 + (2*S^2 + 3*N^2)/2^256 (about 2^-60.4 at qh = qs = 2^64, evaluated outside Lean). column2: SPHINCS_SECURITY_CHARTER (multi-key: adaptive key creation, reordering, overlap, reduction)
column3: Multi-key game mplay: the adversary creates keys adaptively (newKey; key j from seed sd j, generated when asked), signs under any created key, hashes, and claims a forgery (j, m, s); MBudget M qh qk qs. Split at the target i (mplay_split): mplay(sd with s at i) = X >>= (if created then Ygen s >>= Z else Z'), X = mUntil runs until the adversary asks for key i (a point it chooses from its view) and reads only seeds below i, so the target seed enters only through Ygen s; a forgery against key i implies the target was created (leaves_mUntil). Reordering (reorder, generic in the result type): G = X >>= (if c then Y >>= Z else Z') and G' = Y >>= X >>= (if c then Z y else Z'), with the target's key passed on only at the creation point; a tape bijection rotating the fresh-draw blocks of X alone and Y alone (tsum_bij) gives equal results unless X alone and Y alone draw a common request Ov (reorder_point): Pr[created and P(G)] <= Pr[P(G')] + Pr[Ov]. Overlap by provenance (gk_shape, ov_incl): every request of the target's key generation alone is the expansion request of s, the PK.seed or SK.seed key derivation of the expansion output on fresh coordinate p, or keyed by the tweak or PRF key on p+1, p+2; so Ov means a request of X (fixed before p) equals one of five values X never read, each uniform 256-bit at SPX256f; no key-derived collision or structural case arises. ov_count: Pr[Ov] <= A*(3/256^n + 2/256^32) over the target's seed and the tapes, A bounding X's draws (5A/2^256 at SPX256f), not 17185 per request. Reduction (simB, sim_target): the reordered game is, request for request (TagRel, run_tagRel), the single-key real game against redB, which simulates other keys' key generation, signing and claim verification with hash queries (qtA), takes the challenger's pk as key i, and forwards key i's signing queries and claim; redB does not depend on the target's seed. Context injectivity (ekSeedInput_inj): distinct (alg_id, chain_id, h_n, C_pre, k_step) give distinct inputs for any alg_id, as the four 32-byte fields make the total length fix |alg_id|. Domain separation (ekDom_coins): no 'DSM/kyber-coins/v1' input (also keyed by Smaster) is a per-step input. DSM game dplay: adversary gets aux K of Smaster K; asks for the per-step key of contexts it chooses adaptively (a repeated context returns the existing key; at most qn requests), any other Smaster-keyed derivation in full (leak, at most ql; covers the ML-KEM coins), hash queries qh and signing queries qs under any per-step key; claims a forgery. column2: SPHINCS_SECURITY_CHARTER (DSM key schedule KS1: Extract-then-Expand, input injectivity, domain separation)
column3: Key schedule KS1 (core::identity::key_schedule): PRK_w = Extract('DSM/kdf/wallet-root/v1' 0x00, wallet_seed); genesis nonce, GRK seed, AttA, device seed, s0, SDK entropy, recovery AEAD and recovery authority are Expands of PRK_w with info = label 0x00 fields (lp(net) = u32 LE length then bytes; idx, ver, slot u32 LE; G, DevID, aph 32 bytes); PRK_d = Extract('DSM/kdf/device-root/v1' 0x00, device seed) gives the AK seed; PRK_s0 = Extract('DSM/kdf/s0-root/v1' 0x00, s0) gives Smaster and the chain-head at-rest key as sibling Expands; the ML-KEM identity seed is keyed-BLAKE3(Smaster, 'DSM/ml-kem-identity/v1' 0x00 'ML-KEM-768'). HMAC = HMAC-BLAKE3 (RFC 2104), HKDF per RFC 5869. Proved: the three Extract salts are distinct (ks_salts_nodup); the eleven Expand labels are NUL-free and distinct (ksLabels_nul_free, ksLabels_nodup), so label 0x00 determines the label (ksInfo_split); under PRK_w the info determines the node and its whole context for u32 integers and network ids shorter than 2^32 bytes (wnode_info_inj); under PRK_s0 Smaster and the at-rest key are distinct inputs for every context (snode_info_inj); the AK input determines aph (akInfo_inj); the per-step, ML-KEM coins and ML-KEM identity inputs under Smaster are pairwise distinct and the ML-KEM identity input is outside the per-step domain (smaster_inputs_distinct, ekDom_mlkem). dsm_forge_256f_ks1: C67's dsm_forge_256f with aux = [], since under KS1 the ML-KEM identity seed is one of the ql revealed derivations; Adv is the plain PRF advantage of keyed BLAKE3 under Smaster with <= qn + ql queries (an instance of C67; C67 unchanged).
